e7_s4_rationale: The clinical presentation of bilateral cheek swelling, hyperglobus, and expansion of the maxillary ridge, along with the radiographic findings of a well-circumscribed, expansile, heterogeneous mass in the maxillary sinus, is consistent with Cherubism. The age of the patient and the gradual progression of symptoms also support this diagnosis.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Fibrous dysplasia
e7_s4_rejected.why: Fibrous dysplasia typically presents with a ground-glass appearance on radiographs, which is not described in this case.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Juvenile ossifying fibroma
e7_s4_rejected.why: Juvenile ossifying fibroma often presents with a more aggressive clinical course and a characteristic radiographic appearance of a well-defined, radiopaque mass with a sun-ray pattern, which is not described in this case.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Central giant cell granuloma
e7_s4_rejected.why: Central giant cell granuloma typically presents with a more localized lesion and a characteristic radiographic appearance of a well-defined, radiolucent lesion with a soap-bubble appearance, which is not described in this case.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Ewing sarcoma
e7_s4_rejected.why: Ewing sarcoma is a highly aggressive malignancy that typically presents with systemic symptoms, such as fever and weight loss, and a characteristic radiographic appearance of a permeative, destructive lesion with a soft-tissue mass, which is not described in this case.
